[p83]       2.1.     DATA-001 Priceable Entity
[p83] 
[p83] 
[p83] The workspace must support the creation and management of Priceable Entities.
[p83] 
[p83] A Priceable Entity is a business offering to which the organisation can assign or evaluate a
[p83] distinct selling price within an applicable pricing context.
[p83] 
[p83] Supported Priceable Entity types must include, at minimum:
[p83] 
[p83]     ● product;
[p83]     ● SKU or product variant;
[p83]     ● service;
[p83]     ● another organisation-defined directly priceable offering.
[p83] 
[p83] A product may itself be a Priceable Entity where the organisation prices that product directly.
[p83] 
[p83] Where individual SKUs or variants of a product have distinct selling prices, each
[p83] independently priced SKU or variant must be represented as its own Priceable Entity.
[p83] 
[p83] Categories and product groups must not become Priceable Entities solely because they are
[p83] used to organise, filter or apply pricing work across multiple Priceable Entities.
[p83] 
[p83] Pricing dimensions such as location, region, channel, customer group, business unit, vendor
[p83] or price list must remain distinct from the Priceable Entity itself.
[p83] 
[p83] A Priceable Entity may therefore have different Price Records, Cost Records or pricing
[p83] outcomes across supported pricing dimensions without becoming a different Priceable Entity
[p83] unless the organisation's underlying commercial object is itself different.
[p83] 
[p83] Each Priceable Entity must have, at minimum:
[p83] 
[p83]     ● unique Owómidé identifier;
[p83]     ● organisation-defined name;
[p83]     ● entity type;
[p83] 
[p84]       ● status.
[p84] 
[p84] Where available, a Priceable Entity may also contain:
[p84] 
[p84]       ● SKU, product code or external identifier;
[p84]       ● parent product or related organisational grouping;
[p84]       ● category;
[p84]       ● brand;
[p84]       ● base unit of measure;
[p84]       ● description;
[p84]       ● organisation-specific reference fields.
[p84] 
[p84] Currency must be associated with the applicable monetary record or pricing context rather
[p84] than assumed to be an immutable property of the Priceable Entity.
[p84] 
[p84] The Priceable Entity model must remain sufficiently flexible to support organisations that
[p84] price at product, SKU, variant or service level without requiring every organisation to use the
[p84] same catalogue hierarchy.
[p84] 
[p84]

Must.snippet: DATA-001 Priceable Entity The workspace must support the creation and management of Priceable Entities.
Supported Priceable Entity types must include, at minimum: ● product; ● SKU or product variant; ● service; ● another organisation-defined directly priceable offering.
Where individual SKUs or variants of a product have distinct selling prices, each independently priced SKU or variant must be represented as its own Priceable Entity.
Pricing dimensions such as location, region, channel, customer group, business unit, vendor or price list must remain distinct from the Priceable Entity itself.
Each Priceable Entity must have, at minimum: ● unique Owómidé identifier; ● organisation-defined name; ● entity type; ● status.
Currency must be associated with the applicable monetary record or pricing context rather than assumed to be an immutable property of the Priceable Entity.

The Priceable Entity model must remain sufficiently flexible to support organisations that price at product, SKU, variant or service level without requiring every organisation to use the same catalogue hierarchy.

[p84] 
[p84] 
[p84] The system must allow an organisation to maintain structured Price Records for Priceable
[p84] Entities.
[p84] 
[p85] A Price Record represents a selling-price value for a Priceable Entity within a defined pricing
[p85] context.
[p85] 
[p85] Each Price Record must identify, where applicable:
[p85] 
[p85]    ● Priceable Entity;
[p85]    ● price amount;
[p85]    ● currency;
[p85]    ● applicable pricing dimensions;
[p85]    ● effective-from date or timestamp;
[p85]    ● effective-to date or timestamp where applicable;
[p85]    ● source;
[p85]    ● last updated timestamp.
[p85] 
[p85] The system must support different Price Records for the same Priceable Entity where pricing
[p85] legitimately differs by location, channel, customer group, price list, currency or another
[p85] configured pricing dimension.
[p85] 
[p85] The system must also preserve multiple Price Records over time for the same pricing
[p85] context where the selling price changes.
[p85] 
[p85] Current Price means the specific Price Record that is presently applicable to a Priceable
[p85] Entity within the relevant pricing context at the applicable reference time.
[p85] 
[p85] A Current Price must therefore remain associated with:
[p85] 
[p85]    ● the Priceable Entity;
[p85]    ● price amount;
[p85]    ● currency;
[p85]    ● applicable pricing dimensions;
[p85]    ● effective context;
[p85]    ● source Price Record.
[p85] 
[p85] The system must not silently treat the newest Price Record, most recently imported value or
[p85] another arbitrary Price Record as the Current Price where more than one record could apply.
[p85] 
[p85] For the same Priceable Entity and exact pricing context, the system must not represent
[p85] conflicting Price Records as simultaneously being the Current Price for the same reference
[p85] time.
[p85] 
[p86] Where overlapping, conflicting or insufficiently specified Price Records prevent the Current
[p86] Price from being determined unambiguously, the system must identify the Current Price as
[p86] unresolved and require appropriate authorised correction or selection rather than silently
[p86] choosing a value.
[p86] 
[p86] A future-effective Price Record must not become Current Price before its applicable effective
[p86] time.
[p86] 
[p86] A historical Price Record must remain preserved after it ceases to be Current Price.
[p86] 
[p86] Where no applicable Price Record exists, Current Price must be represented as unavailable
[p86] rather than assumed to be zero or inferred from another pricing context.
[p86] 
[p86] Any consequential pricing work that uses Current Price must remain traceable to the exact
[p86] Price Record and pricing context from which that Current Price was determined.

Must.snippet: DATA-006 Manual Data Entry Authorised users must be able to create and update supported pricing-context records manually.
Manual entry must apply the same: ● validation; ● permissions; ● audit; ● provenance; ● historical-integrity requirements as imported or externally supplied pricing data.
Where a user manually enters selling-price information, that information must enter Owómidé through the Price Record model defined in DATA-003.
A manual selling-price change that establishes a new Current Price must preserve the previous Price Record in accordance with DATA-005 rather than overwrite the historical price value.

Where manual entry creates overlapping, conflicting or insufficiently specified Price Records that prevent Current Price from being determined unambiguously, the system must identify the Current Price as unresolved rather than silently selecting a record.
Manual entry of cost information must continue to follow the Cost Record and Applicable Unit Cost requirements defined in DATA-004.

May.snippet: A manually entered price may become the Current Price only where the applicable Priceable Entity, pricing dimensions, currency and effective context are sufficiently identified and the Current Price can be determined without unresolved conflict.

[p92]     2.13.        DATA-013 Pricing Context Snapshot
[p92] 
[p92] 
[p92] When a Pricing Proposal is formally submitted into an organisational decision path, the
[p92] material pricing context used to construct and analyse that Proposal version must be
[p92] preserved as part of its controlled decision basis.
[p92] 
[p92] Where applicable, the preserved pricing context must include:
[p92] 
[p92]    ● the exact Current Price or other Price Record materially used as the pricing baseline,
[p92]        including the source Price Record, applicable pricing dimensions and relevant
[p92]        effective context;
[p92]    ● Applicable Unit Cost used in decision-relevant calculations;
[p92]    ● cost basis associated with that Applicable Unit Cost;
[p92]    ● currency;
[p92]    ● applicable unit of measure;
[p92]    ● source Cost Record or explicit cost assumption;
[p92]    ● applicable pricing dimensions;
[p92]    ● other structured pricing-context values materially used in the analysis;
[p92]    ● relevant source and freshness information.
[p92] 
[p92] Where Current Price formed part of the submitted Proposal's decision basis, the snapshot
[p92] must preserve the exact Price Record that represented Current Price for that pricing context
[p92] rather than retaining only an untraceable numeric price value.
[p92] 
[p92] Where an explicit assumed cost is used instead of a structured Cost Record, the snapshot

[p93] 
[p93] When creating or developing a Pricing Initiative, authorised users must be able to define the

[p93]    ● channel;
[p93]    ● customer group;
[p93]    ● business unit;
[p93]    ● vendor;
[p93]    ● price list;

[p93] 
[p93] A category, product group or pricing dimension used for scope selection must remain
[p93] distinguishable from the Priceable Entities included through that selection.
[p93] 
[p93] The system must allow users to understand both:
[p93] 
[p93]    ● how the scope was selected; and
[p93]    ● which Priceable Entities and pricing-dimension combinations are currently included.
[p93] 
[p93] Before a Pricing Proposal is formally submitted, the affected scope must resolve to an
[p93] explicit set of Priceable Entities and applicable pricing dimensions.
[p93] 
[p94] The system must not submit a Proposal whose affected commercial scope cannot be
[p94] determined.

[p94]     2.16.     DATA-016 Data Validation
[p94] 
[p94] 
[p94] The system must validate structured pricing data before it is used in calculations or
[p94] submitted as part of formal pricing work.
[p94] 
[p94] Validation should detect relevant issues including:
[p94] 
[p94]    ● missing required values;
[p94]    ● invalid numeric formats;
[p94]    ● unsupported currencies;
[p94]    ● negative values where not permitted;
[p94]    ● inconsistent pricing scope;
[p94]    ● duplicate records;

[p96]     2.21.      DATA-021 Bounded External Data Integration
[p96] 
[p96] 
[p96] The MVP must support a bounded external data-integration capability for selected business
[p96] or productivity systems where direct connectivity materially reduces the effort required to
[p96] establish or maintain pricing context.
[p96] 
[p96] Supported integrations may provide access to relevant information such as:
[p96] 
[p96]    ● priceable entities and external identifiers;
[p96]    ● product or service attributes;
[p96]    ● Price Records, including current-known prices where supplied;
[p96]    ● cost information where authorised, including the available cost amount, cost basis,
[p96]          currency, unit or cost unit, applicable pricing dimensions and effective context;
[p96]    ● categories and other pricing dimensions;
[p96] 
[p97]    ● other supported pricing-context fields.
[p97] 
[p97] Where an external integration supplies cost information, that information must enter
[p97] Owómidé through the Cost Record model defined in DATA-004.
[p97] 
[p97] Where an external integration supplies selling-price information, that information must enter
[p97] Owómidé through the Price Record model defined in DATA-003.
[p97] 
[p97] An externally supplied value described as a current price may become the Current Price only
[p97] where its Priceable Entity, pricing dimensions, currency and effective applicability are
[p97] sufficiently identified and no unresolved conflicting Price Record prevents a unique
[p97] determination.
[p97] 
[p97] Receipt of a newer external price value must not by itself cause Owómidé to silently replace
[p97] the existing Current Price.
[p97] 
[p97] An externally supplied cost value must not automatically become the Applicable Unit Cost
[p97] solely because it was received from an integrated system.
[p97] 
[p97] Selection or determination of the Applicable Unit Cost for consequential pricing calculations
[p97] must continue to follow DATA-004, including applicable cost-basis, unit, currency,
[p97] pricing-dimension and ambiguity requirements.
[p97] 
[p97] At least one external connector should be supported as part of the MVP, with the specific
[p97] system selected according to validated customer or pilot requirements.
[p97] 
[p97] Additional connectors must not automatically become MVP requirements.
[p97] 
[p97] Data received through an external integration must:
[p97] 
[p97]    ● pass applicable Owómidé validation rules;
[p97]    ● preserve its originating source;
[p97]    ● preserve the relevant retrieval or synchronisation timestamp;
[p97]    ● respect workspace permissions and sensitive-data controls;
[p97]    ● distinguish externally sourced information from manually entered information;
[p97]    ● avoid being represented as real-time where the integration does not provide real-time
[p97]        data.
[p97] 
[p97] Failure or unavailability of an external integration must not corrupt existing pricing records or
[p97] prevent use of supported manual or structured-import alternatives.
[p97] 
[p98] The MVP does not require universal bidirectional synchronisation with external business
[p98] systems.
[p98]

[p105]      3.12.     INIT-012 Initiative Context Aggregation
[p105] 
[p105] 
[p105] The Pricing Initiative must provide a coherent view of the decision-relevant information
[p105] associated with the pricing work without creating a separate competing information type
[p105] called Initiative Context.
[p105] 
[p105] The Initiative may surface or reference, according to the user's permissions:
[p105] 
[p105]     ● structured Product and Pricing Context governed by Section 3.2;
[p105]     ● supporting Evidence governed by Section 3.7;
[p105]     ● explicit Assumptions governed by INIT-013, BUILD-008 and ANALYSIS-017;
[p105]     ● the pricing objective and business rationale;
[p105]     ● relevant Pricing Builder work;
[p105]     ● analysis and Scenarios;
[p105]     ● Pricing Proposals;
[p105]     ● collaboration and review activity;
[p105]     ● workflow and organisational decision information;
[p105]     ● execution and monitoring information where applicable.
[p105] 
[p105] Information surfaced through the Initiative must retain its originating product object,
[p105] information type, source, provenance and relevant version context.
[p105] 
[p105] Displaying information within a Pricing Initiative must not:
[p105] 
[p106]    ● convert supporting Evidence into authoritative structured Pricing Context;
[p106]    ● convert an Assumption into verified organisational data;
[p106]    ● convert a comment or discussion into Evidence merely because it is visible within the
[p106]          Initiative;
[p106]    ● create a second copy of a structured Price Record, Cost Record or other canonical
[p106]          Pricing Context record.
[p106] 
[p106] Supporting documents, observations, market information, stakeholder feedback and similar
[p106] supporting material must be managed as Evidence under Section 3.7 where they are
[p106] intended to support or challenge pricing work.
[p106] 
[p106] Structured pricing information intended to operate as authoritative Owómidé Pricing Context
[p106] must follow the applicable requirements in Section 3.2.
[p106] 
[p106] The Pricing Initiative therefore acts as the organising container and contextual view across
[p106] these information classes rather than becoming a separate canonical owner of them.
[p106]

[p106]     3.13.        INIT-013 Initiative-Level Assumptions
[p106] 
[p106] 
[p106] Users must be able to record explicit Assumptions that materially influence pricing work.
[p106] 
[p106] An Assumption is an explicitly identified premise, estimate or working value relied upon
[p106] where:
[p106] 
[p106]    ● verified information is unavailable;
[p106]    ● an alternative condition is deliberately being tested;
[p106]    ● a Scenario requires a hypothetical input; or
[p106]    ● organisational judgement is intentionally being used instead of verified structured
[p106]          information.
[p106] 
[p106] An Assumption must remain distinguishable from:
[p106] 
[p106]    ● structured Pricing Context governed by Section 3.2;
[p106]    ● supporting Evidence governed by Section 3.7;
[p106]    ● verified organisational data;
[p106]    ● AI inference;
[p106]    ● comments or stakeholder discussion;
[p106]    ● pricing parameters or commercial targets that are known rather than assumed.
[p106] 
[p106] Where applicable, a material Assumption should identify:
[p106] 
[p107]    ● the assumed value, condition or premise;
[p107]    ● the user responsible for introducing it;
[p107]    ● the pricing work, Scenario, calculation or Pricing Scope to which it applies;
[p107]    ● the reason or basis for the Assumption;
[p107]    ● supporting Evidence where available;
[p107]    ● creation or application timestamp;
[p107]    ● relevant version context.
[p107] 
[p107] Evidence may support an Assumption without converting that Assumption into verified
[p107] organisational data.
[p107] 
[p107] Where verified information later replaces an Assumption in current pricing work, historical
[p107] controlled versions must continue to preserve the Assumption that formed part of their
[p107] original decision basis.
[p107] 
[p107] Important Assumptions must not exist solely inside comments, attachments or AI
[p107] conversations.
[p107] 
[p107] Material Assumptions relied upon by a submitted Pricing Proposal must remain preserved
[p107] with the applicable controlled Proposal version in accordance with PROP-011.
[p107] 
[p107]

Must.snippet: INIT-018 Hold and Cancel Authorised users must be able to place a Pricing Initiative On Hold or Cancel it.

On Hold must temporarily pause progression without deleting or resetting the initiative's existing lifecycle context.
Cancelled initiatives must retain their existing pricing work and history.

Expiration of a Pricing Proposal version or loss of current execution authority must be handled through the applicable Proposal-validity, workflow and governance requirements rather than through the Pricing Initiative lifecycle.

[p114]        4.5.     BUILD-005 Structured Pricing Logic
[p114] 
[p114] 
[p114] The MVP must represent pricing logic using structured components rather than free-text
[p114] instructions alone.
[p114] 
[p114] Supported Builder-owned components must include, where applicable:
[p114] 
[p114]     ● action;
[p114]     ● input;
[p114]     ● operator;
[p114]     ● value;
[p114]     ● condition;
[p114]     ● threshold contained within the pricing logic;
[p114]     ● initiative-specific constraint;
[p114]     ● effective period.
[p114] 
[p114] For example:
[p114] 
[p114] Increase current selling price by 8% provided resulting gross margin remains at or above
[p114] 15%.
[p114] 
[p115] Where a condition or threshold is created specifically for the Pricing Initiative, it must remain
[p115] an initiative-specific condition or constraint unless it references an existing organisational
[p115] Guardrail configured under GOV-023.
[p115] 
[p115] Organisational Guardrails must not be created or redefined merely by including a threshold,
[p115] condition or constraint in Builder pricing logic.
[p115] 
[p115] Where pricing work is subject to an organisational Guardrail, the Builder must reference the
[p115] applicable Guardrail from the governance layer and consume its authoritative evaluation in
[p115] accordance with BUILD-010 and ANALYSIS-014.
[p115] 
[p115] The underlying Builder structure must remain machine-readable while the user-facing
[p115] representation remains understandable to business users.

[p117]     4.10.     BUILD-010 Guardrails and Initiative-Specific Constraints
[p117] 
[p117] 
[p117] Pricing work in the Builder must respect applicable organisational Guardrails and any

[p117]

[p117]    ● the evaluated pricing value or metric;
[p117]    ● the configured behavioural treatment.

[p117] 
[p117]    ● conditions;
[p117]    ● commercial targets;
[p117]

[p118]     ● constraints.

[p121] or an AI-generated estimate.

[p124]     4.22.      BUILD-022 Builder Validation
[p124] 
[p124] 
[p124] Before pricing work can become part of a formal Pricing Proposal, the Builder must validate
[p124] that the Builder-owned pricing work is sufficiently defined for its intended pricing action.
[p124] 
[p124] Validation must include, where applicable:
[p124] 
[p124]    ● Pricing Scope exists;
[p124]    ● pricing action is defined;
[p124]    ● required calculation inputs are available or explicitly identified as assumptions;
[p124]    ● required operators and deterministic calculation methods are supported;
[p124]    ● numeric inputs satisfy applicable formula constraints;
[p124]    ● calculated outputs are valid;
[p124]    ● qualitative or non-deterministically evaluated components are explicitly
[p124]        distinguishable from calculated outputs;
[p124]    ● assumptions are explicit;
[p124]    ● initiative-specific conditions and constraints are sufficiently defined;
[p124]    ● applicable organisational Guardrails have been identified;
[p124]    ● authoritative Guardrail evaluations are available where the required analytical inputs
[p124]        exist;
[p124]    ● no unresolved Builder-owned validation error remains.
[p124] 
[p124] Where an applicable organisational Guardrail has been evaluated, the Builder must surface
[p124] the ANALYSIS-014 result rather than calculate an alternative Guardrail result.
[p124] 
[p124] The Builder must not independently determine whether a Warning, Approval Escalation,
[p124] Blocking Breach or Unable to Evaluate result permits formal Proposal submission.
[p124] 
[p124] Guardrail behavioural treatment is governed by GOV-025.
[p124] 
[p124] Formal Proposal submission readiness is governed by PROP-009.
[p124] 
[p124] The Builder must not treat unsupported custom logic as though it had been deterministically
[p124] calculated.
[p124] 
[p125] Where non-deterministic pricing logic is permitted to progress, its manually determined,
[p125] qualitative or unsupported components must remain explicit for subsequent analysis, review
[p125] and organisational decision.
[p125] 
[p125]

source.exactNormativeText:
[p130]       5.4.     ANALYSIS-004 Gross Margin and Target-Margin Price Calculation
[p130] 
[p130] 
[p130] Where the selling price and the Applicable Unit Cost defined in DATA-004 are available, the
[p130] gross margin percentage must be calculated as:
[p130] 
[p130] Gross Margin % = ((Selling Price - Applicable Unit Cost) / Selling Price) × 100
[p130] 
[p130] This calculation is valid only where Selling Price is greater than zero.
[p130] 
[p130] The system must distinguish gross margin from markup.
[p130] 
[p130] Where a user defines a target gross-margin percentage and the Applicable Unit Cost defined
[p130] in DATA-004 is available and greater than zero, the system must deterministically derive the
[p130] corresponding proposed selling price as:
[p130] 
[p130] Proposed Selling Price = Applicable Unit Cost / (1 - (Target Gross Margin % / 100))
[p130] 
[p131] The target gross-margin percentage used in this calculation must be less than 100%.
[p131] 
[p131] Where the target gross-margin percentage is equal to or greater than 100%, or the required
[p131] Applicable Unit Cost is unavailable or invalid, the system must not produce a derived
[p131] proposed selling price and must identify why the calculation cannot be completed.
[p131] 
[p131] Where organisational policy permits a negative target gross margin, the calculation may
[p131] proceed provided the required inputs are valid and the resulting price satisfies applicable
[p131] guardrails.
[p131] 
[p131] The system must preserve the Applicable Unit Cost, cost basis, source Cost Record or
[p131] explicit cost assumption, target gross-margin percentage, formula and resulting unrounded
[p131] proposed selling price used in the calculation.
[p131] 
[p131] Any displayed or executable price rounding must follow the applicable pricing precision and
[p131] rounding rules rather than silently changing the underlying target-margin calculation.
[p131] 
[p131]

[p130]       5.4.     ANALYSIS-004 Gross Margin and Target-Margin Price Calculation
[p130] 
[p130] 
[p130] Where the selling price and the Applicable Unit Cost defined in DATA-004 are available, the
[p130] gross margin percentage must be calculated as:
[p130] 
[p130] Gross Margin % = ((Selling Price - Applicable Unit Cost) / Selling Price) × 100
[p130] 
[p130] This calculation is valid only where Selling Price is greater than zero.
[p130] 
[p130] The system must distinguish gross margin from markup.
[p130] 
[p130] Where a user defines a target gross-margin percentage and the Applicable Unit Cost defined
[p130] in DATA-004 is available and greater than zero, the system must deterministically derive the
[p130] corresponding proposed selling price as:
[p130] 
[p130] Proposed Selling Price = Applicable Unit Cost / (1 - (Target Gross Margin % / 100))
[p130] 
[p131] The target gross-margin percentage used in this calculation must be less than 100%.
[p131] 
[p131] Where the target gross-margin percentage is equal to or greater than 100%, or the required
[p131] Applicable Unit Cost is unavailable or invalid, the system must not produce a derived
[p131] proposed selling price and must identify why the calculation cannot be completed.
[p131] 
[p131] Where organisational policy permits a negative target gross margin, the calculation may
[p131] proceed provided the required inputs are valid and the resulting price satisfies applicable
[p131] guardrails.
[p131] 
[p131] The system must preserve the Applicable Unit Cost, cost basis, source Cost Record or
[p131] explicit cost assumption, target gross-margin percentage, formula and resulting unrounded
[p131] proposed selling price used in the calculation.
[p131] 
[p131] Any displayed or executable price rounding must follow the applicable pricing precision and
[p131] rounding rules rather than silently changing the underlying target-margin calculation.
[p131] 
[p131]

source.exactNormativeText:
[p132]       5.6.    ANALYSIS-006 Price Adjustment and Price Change Calculation
[p132] 
[p132] 
[p132] Where a pricing action derives a proposed selling price from a baseline price, the baseline
[p132] used by the calculation must be explicitly identifiable.
[p132] 
[p132] The baseline may be the current selling price or another supported pricing baseline explicitly
[p132] defined by the pricing action.
[p132] 
[p132] Where the baseline is Current Price, the calculation must use the Current Price defined in
[p132] DATA-003 for the affected Priceable Entity and pricing context.
[p132] 
[p132] Where no unambiguous Current Price exists, the system must not silently select another
[p132] Price Record as Current Price.
[p132] 
[p132] An authorised user may define another supported pricing baseline where the pricing action
[p132] permits it, but that baseline must remain explicitly distinguishable from Current Price.
[p132] 
[p132] Where:
[p132] 
[p132] Baseline Price = B
[p132] 
[p132] Percentage Adjustment = R
[p132] 
[p132] Absolute Adjustment = A
[p132] 
[p132] the MVP must support the following deterministic calculations where applicable.
[p132] 
[p132] For a percentage increase:
[p132] 
[p132] Proposed Selling Price = B × (1 + (R / 100))
[p132] 
[p133] For a percentage decrease:
[p133] 
[p133] Proposed Selling Price = B × (1 - (R / 100))
[p133] 
[p133] For an absolute-value increase:
[p133] 
[p133] Proposed Selling Price = B + A
[p133] 
[p133] For an absolute-value decrease:
[p133] 
[p133] Proposed Selling Price = B - A
[p133] 
[p133] For promotional, discount or markdown pricing expressed as a percentage reduction:
[p133] 
[p133] Proposed Selling Price = B × (1 - (Discount % / 100))
[p133] 
[p133] For promotional, discount or markdown pricing expressed as an absolute-value reduction:
[p133] 
[p133] Proposed Selling Price = B - Discount Amount
[p133] 
[p133] Percentage reductions must not be less than 0% or greater than 100%.
[p133] 
[p133] Absolute reductions must not produce a negative proposed selling price.
[p133] 
[p133] Where a promotional, markdown or other pricing action directly specifies the final selling
[p133] price rather than an adjustment, that value must be treated as the proposed selling price
[p133] rather than recalculated through an adjustment formula.
[p133] 
[p133] After the proposed selling price is determined, the system must calculate price change
[p133] against Current Price where an unambiguous Current Price is available under DATA-003.
[p133] 
[p133] Where Current Price is available:
[p133] 
[p133] Absolute Price Change = Proposed Price - Current Price
[p133] 
[p133] and, where Current Price is not zero:
[p133] 
[p133] Price Change % = ((Proposed Price - Current Price) / Current Price) × 100
[p133] 
[p133] Where Current Price is zero, percentage price change must be represented as unavailable
[p133] rather than producing an undefined or misleading percentage.
[p133] 
[p133] Where Current Price is unavailable or unresolved, absolute and percentage change against
[p133] Current Price must be represented as unavailable.
[p133] 
[p134] Unavailability of Current Price must not prevent a pricing action from being deterministically
[p134] calculated where that action validly uses another explicitly identified pricing baseline and all
[p134] inputs required for that calculation are available.
[p134] 
[p134] Where the product displays a change relative to an alternative pricing baseline, that result
[p134] must be explicitly identified as change relative to that baseline and must not be labelled as
[p134] change from Current Price.
[p134] 
[p134] The system must preserve the pricing action, baseline value, baseline type, adjustment
[p134] value, calculation method and resulting proposed selling price used in the calculation.
[p134] 
[p134] Where Current Price is the baseline, the preserved calculation context must remain
[p134] traceable to the exact source Price Record defined under DATA-003.
[p134] 
[p134]

[p137]      5.14.    ANALYSIS-014 Deterministic Guardrail Evaluation
[p137] 
[p137] 
[p137] The analytical layer must perform deterministic evaluation of applicable organisational
[p137] Guardrails defined under GOV-023 where the required structured pricing information is
[p137] available.
[p137] 
[p138] The analytical layer must not independently create Guardrails, determine Guardrail
[p138] applicability or redefine their configured behavioural treatment.
[p138] 
[p138] Those responsibilities remain governed by GOV-023, GOV-024 and GOV-025.
[p138] 
[p138] For each applicable Guardrail, supported evaluation states must include:
[p138] 
[p138]     ● Within Guardrail;
[p138]     ● Breach;
[p138]     ● Unable to Evaluate.
[p138] 
[p138] Near Threshold may additionally be displayed only where the applicable Guardrail
[p138] configuration defines a supported proximity threshold or warning band sufficient to determine
[p138] that state consistently.
[p138] 
[p138] Near Threshold must not be inferred from an undefined or arbitrary proximity rule.
[p138] 
[p138] Each material Guardrail evaluation must preserve enough information to determine, where
[p138] applicable:
[p138] 
[p138]     ● Guardrail identifier;
[p138]     ● applicable Guardrail configuration version;
[p138]     ● affected Priceable Entity or Pricing Scope;
[p138]     ● applicable pricing dimensions;
[p138]     ● metric or pricing condition evaluated;
[p138]     ● operator or comparison rule;
[p138]     ● configured threshold or value;
[p138]     ● actual pricing value or calculated metric evaluated;
[p138]     ● relevant source inputs or assumptions;
[p138]     ● evaluation state;
[p138]     ● evaluation timestamp.
[p138] 
[p138] Where required information is missing, invalid or incompatible, the evaluation state must be
[p138] Unable to Evaluate.
[p138] 
[p138] Unable to Evaluate must not be represented as Within Guardrail.
[p138] 
[p138] The analytical layer must return the evaluation result to the consuming product capabilities.
[p138] 
[p138] The governance consequence of a Breach must follow the behavioural treatment configured
[p138] under GOV-025 rather than being independently determined by the analytical layer.
[p138] 
[p139] Where multiple Guardrails apply to the same pricing work, each Guardrail must be evaluated
[p139] and preserved separately.
[p139] 
[p139] Aggregate analysis must not conceal an entity-level Guardrail Breach or Unable to Evaluate
[p139] result.
[p139]

[p139]      5.15.      ANALYSIS-015 Margin Floor Validation
[p139] 
[p139] 
[p139] Where an organisation has configured a minimum gross-margin threshold, the system must
[p139] evaluate the proposed selling price against that threshold using the Applicable Unit Cost
[p139] defined in DATA-004.
[p139] 
[p139] The margin-floor evaluation must use the same Applicable Unit Cost and cost basis as the
[p139] decision-relevant gross-margin analysis for that pricing action.
[p139] 
[p139] Where no valid Applicable Unit Cost is available, or where the applicable cost cannot be
[p139] determined because multiple Cost Records remain unresolved, the margin-floor guardrail
[p139] must be represented as Unable to Evaluate rather than as passed or breached.
[p139] 
[p139] Where an explicit assumed Applicable Unit Cost is permitted and used, that assumption
[p139] must remain visible and attributable during the guardrail evaluation.
[p139] 
[p139] A confirmed breach must remain visible during:
[p139] 
[p139]     ● analysis;
[p139]     ● review;
[p139]     ● Proposal creation;
[p139]     ● the applicable organisational decision process.
[p139] 
[p139] The system must not hide a breach because the Proposal is otherwise complete.
[p139] 
[p139] A change to the Applicable Unit Cost or cost basis that materially changes the margin-floor
[p139] result must be treated as a consequential change to the decision basis.
[p139] 
[p139]

[p144]     5.26.     ANALYSIS-026 Analytical Completeness for Proposal Preparation
[p144] 
[p144] 
[p144] Before analysed pricing work is used to prepare a formal Pricing Proposal, the analytical
[p144] layer must determine whether the decision-relevant analysis is sufficiently complete to
[p144] support Proposal preparation.
[p144] 
[p144] The analytical completeness check must identify, where applicable:
[p144] 
[p144]    ● unresolved calculation errors;
[p144]    ● missing required financial inputs;
[p144]    ● calculations that remain unavailable;
[p144]    ● invalid pricing outputs;
[p144]    ● material assumptions that are undefined or insufficiently identified;
[p144]    ● applicable Guardrails that remain Unable to Evaluate because required analytical
[p144]        information is missing or invalid.
[p144] 
[p144] A Guardrail Breach is an analytical evaluation result and must not automatically be
[p144] represented as an analytical error.
[p144] 
[p144] The governance consequence of a Guardrail Breach is determined by the configured
[p144] behavioural treatment under GOV-025.
[p144] 
[p145] The analytical layer must not independently determine whether a Pricing Proposal may be
[p145] submitted.
[p145] 
[p145] Formal Proposal submission readiness, including treatment of Warning, Approval Escalation,
[p145] Blocking and Unable to Evaluate Guardrail results, is governed by PROP-009.
[p145] 
[p145] Analytical completeness must therefore supply authoritative analysis and Guardrail
[p145] evaluation information to Proposal readiness without becoming a second owner of
[p145] submission policy.
[p145] 
[p145]

[p150] 
[p150] 
[p150] An authorised user must be able to create a Pricing Proposal from sufficiently developed
[p150] pricing work within a Pricing Initiative.
[p150] 
[p150] Proposal creation may use:
[p150] 
[p150]     ● pricing work constructed directly in the Pricing Builder;
[p150]     ● a Scenario deliberately selected as the basis for progression;
[p150]     ● another supported pricing approach developed within the Initiative.
[p150] 
[p150] Creating a Pricing Proposal must create the initial Proposal version in Draft status.
[p150] 
[p150] The Draft Proposal version may be edited by authorised users until it is formally submitted
[p150] into an applicable organisational decision path.
[p150] 
[p150] Formal submission must freeze that same Draft Proposal version as the controlled decision
[p150] package used for either item-level approval or configured policy authorisation.
[p150] 
[p151] Submission must not create a second Proposal version solely because the existing Draft
[p151] Proposal version enters a decision path.
[p151] 
[p151] Proposal creation must not by itself:
[p151] 
[p151]     ● submit the Proposal into an organisational decision path;
[p151]     ● create an approval;
[p151]     ● provide policy authorisation;
[p151]     ● authorise execution;
[p151]     ● modify the organisation's current price;
[p151]     ● trigger implementation.
[p151]

[p153]       6.8.    PROP-008 Scenario and Proposal Separation
[p153] 
[p153] 
[p153] A Scenario and a Pricing Proposal must remain separate product objects.
[p153] 
[p153] A Scenario represents an alternative pricing approach under consideration.
[p153] 
[p153] A Pricing Proposal represents the specific action being submitted for organisational decision.
[p153] 
[p153] Selecting a Scenario may establish it as the basis for Proposal creation, but Scenario
[p153] selection must not itself:
[p153] 
[p153]    ● create approval or policy-authorisation authority;
[p153]    ● make the Scenario an authorised pricing action;
[p153]    ● trigger execution;
[p153]    ● replace the formal Proposal process.
[p153] 
[p153] A Pricing Proposal may also be created without a Scenario where the pricing action was
[p153] developed directly through the Pricing Builder.
[p153] 
[p153]

[p153]       6.9.    PROP-009 Proposal Readiness
[p153] 
[p153] 
[p153] Before a Pricing Proposal can be formally submitted, the system must determine whether
[p153] the Proposal is sufficiently complete for organisational decision.
[p153] 
[p153] Readiness must consider applicable requirements including:
[p153] 
[p153]    ● defined Pricing Scope;
[p153]    ● defined pricing action;
[p153]    ● valid pricing logic;
[p153]    ● required pricing inputs;
[p153] 
[p154]     ● required analysis;
[p154]     ● explicit material assumptions;
[p154]     ● applicable Guardrail evaluations produced under ANALYSIS-014;
[p154]     ● configured Guardrail behavioural treatment under GOV-025;
[p154]     ● required effective timing;
[p154]     ● unresolved blocking errors;
[p154]     ● required organisational decision information.
[p154] 
[p154] Proposal readiness must consume the authoritative Guardrail evaluation and configured
[p154] behavioural treatment rather than independently recalculating or redefining Guardrail status.
[p154] 
[p154] Where an applicable Guardrail result is Breach:
[p154] 
[p154]     ● Warning treatment may permit submission where all other readiness requirements
[p154]         are satisfied, but the Breach must remain visible;
[p154]     ● Approval Escalation treatment must preserve the requirement for the applicable
[p154]         escalated organisational decision path;
[p154]     ● Blocking treatment must prevent submission where the applicable controlled gate
[p154]         does not permit progression.
[p154] 
[p154] Where a Guardrail required for the organisational decision is Unable to Evaluate, the
[p154] Proposal must not be treated as ready unless the applicable organisational policy explicitly
[p154] permits progression without that evaluation.
[p154] 
[p154] Missing or blocking readiness requirements must be clearly identified to the user.
[p154] 
[p154] A Proposal that fails a blocking readiness requirement must not be submitted.
[p154] 
[p154] Proposal readiness must not independently redefine Guardrail configuration, evaluation
[p154] logic, approval authority or policy-authorisation eligibility.
[p154] 
[p154]

[p155]      6.11.    PROP-011 Proposal Submission and Decision Snapshot
[p155] 
[p155] 
[p155] When a Pricing Proposal is formally submitted into an applicable organisational decision
[p155] path, the system must freeze the current Draft Proposal version as the controlled decision
[p155] snapshot representing the exact decision package presented for item-level approval or
[p155] policy authorisation.
[p155] 
[p155] Formal submission must not create an additional Proposal version solely because the
[p155] existing Draft Proposal version entered the decision process.
[p155] 
[p155] The submitted Proposal version must preserve, where applicable:
[p155] 
[p155]    ● Proposal identifier and version;
[p155]    ● originating Pricing Initiative;
[p155]    ● organisational decision path;
[p155]    ● exact resolved affected Pricing Scope, including the Priceable Entities and applicable
[p155]        pricing dimensions covered by the submitted Proposal version;
[p155]    ● current or baseline pricing state used;
[p155]    ● decision-relevant pricing context governed by DATA-013, including the Applicable
[p155]        Unit Cost and cost basis where cost-dependent analysis informed the Proposal;
[p155]    ● proposed pricing action;
[p155]    ● proposed prices or pricing logic;
[p155]    ● material assumptions;
[p155]    ● decision-relevant analysis;
[p155]    ● calculated outputs;
[p155]    ● applicable Guardrail identifiers, configuration versions, configured behavioural
[p155]        treatments and ANALYSIS-014 evaluation results;
[p155]    ● material exceptions;
[p155]    ● supporting evidence references;
[p155]    ● intended effective date or effective period;
[p155]    ● submitting user;
[p155]    ● submission timestamp;
[p155]    ● applicable workflow, approval or policy-authorisation requirements;
[p155] 
[p156]    ● applicable policy and qualification evaluation where a policy-authorisation path is
[p156]        used.
[p156] 
[p156] Subsequent changes to underlying workspace data must not silently modify, recalculate or
[p156] reinterpret the submitted Proposal version or its decision snapshot.
[p156] 
[p156] The Guardrail information preserved with the submitted Proposal version must represent the
[p156] exact Guardrail configuration and evaluation that formed part of the decision package at
[p156] submission.
[p156] 
[p156] Subsequent     creation,   modification,   activation,   deactivation   or replacement of an
[p156] organisational Guardrail must not silently change the Guardrail configuration, behavioural
[p156] treatment or evaluation preserved with that submitted Proposal version.
[p156] 
[p156] Where the organisation requires a changed Guardrail configuration to become part of the
[p156] decision basis for already submitted pricing work, that treatment must be explicit and must
[p156] follow the applicable material-change and controlled-version requirements.
[p156] 
[p156] Where a category, product group or another grouping selector was used to establish the
[p156] Pricing Scope, the submitted Proposal version must preserve both the selector used and the
[p156] exact Priceable Entity set resolved at submission.
[p156] 
[p156] Subsequent changes to category membership, product-group membership or other grouping
[p156] relationships must not add Priceable Entities to, remove Priceable Entities from or otherwise
[p156] change the affected scope of the already submitted Proposal version.
[p156] 
[p156] A material change after submission must follow PROP-017.
[p156] 
[p156] Any approval or policy authorisation must bind to this exact controlled Proposal version in
[p156] accordance with PROP-021.
[p156] 
[p156]

[p156] 
[p156] 
[p156] The MVP must support the following Pricing Proposal statuses:
[p156] 
[p156]    ● Draft;
[p156]    ● Awaiting Approval;
[p156]    ● Changes Requested;
[p156]    ● Rejected;
[p156]    ● Approved;
[p156] 
[p157]    ● Authorised Within Policy.
[p157] 
[p157] These statuses represent the decision-processing condition of the applicable Proposal
[p157] version.
[p157] 
[p157] Formal submission into an item-level approval workflow must change the applicable
[p157] controlled Proposal version from Draft to Awaiting Approval.
[p157] 
[p157] Where a current Draft Proposal version is instead validly authorised through a configured
[p157] policy-authorisation path, that same controlled Proposal version must change from Draft to
[p157] Authorised Within Policy in accordance with the applicable policy and governance
[p157] requirements.
[p157] 
[p157] A Proposal version must not simultaneously be represented as Awaiting Approval and
[p157] Authorised Within Policy.
[p157] 
[p157] Where policy authorisation is not granted and item-level approval is required, the Proposal
[p157] must enter Awaiting Approval when it is submitted into the applicable approval workflow.
[p157] 
[p157] Execution states such as Implemented must not be represented as Proposal statuses.
[p157] 
[p157] Pricing Initiative lifecycle states must remain separate from Pricing Proposal statuses.
[p157]

[p157]     6.13.      PROP-013 Proposal Version Validity
[p157] 
[p157] 
[p157] The system must separately identify whether a Proposal version is currently applicable, has
[p157] been superseded or has expired.
[p157] 
[p157] Applicable Proposal version validity states are:
[p157] 
[p157]    ● Current;
[p157]    ● Superseded;
[p157]    ● Expired.
[p157] 
[p157] Proposal version validity must remain separate from Proposal status.
[p157] 
[p157] Current means that the version is the presently applicable Proposal version within the
[p157] Pricing Initiative. It does not by itself mean that the Proposal is approved, authorised or
[p157] executable.
[p157] 
[p158] Superseded means that another Proposal version has replaced it as the currently applicable
[p158] version.
[p158] 
[p158] Expired means that the Proposal version is no longer valid for current progression or
[p158] execution because its applicable validity period, effective window or organisational validity
[p158] condition has ended.
[p158] 
[p158] A Proposal version's validity state must not overwrite the historical Proposal status or
[p158] decision recorded against that version.
[p158] 
[p158] For example, an Approved Proposal that later expires must remain historically identifiable as
[p158] Approved while also being identifiable as Expired.
[p158] 
[p158]

[p159]     6.17.      PROP-017 Material Proposal Change
[p159] 
[p159] 
[p159] After formal submission into an organisational decision path, a material change to a Pricing
[p159] Proposal must not modify the submitted Proposal version in place.
[p159] 
[p159] Material changes include changes to relevant:
[p159] 
[p159]    ● pricing scope;
[p159]    ● pricing action;
[p159]    ● proposed price;
[p159]    ● pricing logic;
[p159]    ● consequential assumptions;
[p159]    ● key financial inputs, including the applicable unit cost or cost basis where a change
[p159]        materially alters the pricing outcome, financial analysis, guardrail result, or decision
[p159]        basis;
[p159]    ● decision-relevant change in applicable Guardrail configuration or ANALYSIS-014
[p159]        evaluation where that change materially alters the Proposal decision basis;
[p159]    ● material exceptions;
[p159]    ● effective pricing action or timing.
[p159] 
[p160] Organisational Guardrail configuration remains governed by GOV-023 and GOV-034 and
[p160] must not be treated as editable Proposal content.
[p160] 
[p160] Where a changed organisational Guardrail configuration is explicitly required to become part
[p160] of the decision basis for already submitted pricing work and that change materially alters the
[p160] applicable Guardrail evaluation, behavioural treatment or organisational decision basis, the
[p160] affected pricing work must proceed through a new controlled Proposal version under this
[p160] requirement.
[p160] 
[p160] A later Guardrail configuration change must not silently modify the existing submitted
[p160] Proposal version or its preserved decision snapshot.
[p160] 
[p160] A material change must create a new controlled Proposal version.
[p160] 
[p160] The new Proposal version must complete the applicable organisational decision
[p160] requirements before it can receive execution authority. Depending on the applicable decision
[p160] path, this may include required review, item-level approval or policy-authorisation evaluation.
[p160] 
[p160] Approval or policy authorisation attached to an earlier Proposal version must not transfer to
[p160] the materially revised Proposal version.
[p160] 
[p160] Previous decisions must remain attached to the exact Proposal version against which they
[p160] were originally made.
[p160] 
[p160] Material-change treatment must remain consistent with PROP-019 where the new Proposal
[p160] version supersedes a previous current version.
[p160]

[p180] 
[p180] 
[p180] The system must determine required approvers using configured organisational workflow
[p180] and authority rules.
[p180] 
[p180] Approval routing must use pricing-specific condition types supported by the MVP.
[p180] 
[p180] Administrators must not define arbitrary executable code, scripts, formulas or unrestricted
[p180] custom expressions for approval routing.
[p180] 
[p180] Routing configuration must select and combine supported organisational decision criteria
[p180] rather than operate as a general rules engine.
[p180] 
[p180] Routing may depend on supported decision information such as:

[p181]    ● channel;

[p181]        Guardrail Breach.
[p181] 
[p181] Where routing depends on Guardrail information, the workflow system must consume the
[p181] authoritative ANALYSIS-014 evaluation and GOV-025 behavioural treatment.
[p181]

[p181] Guardrail threshold or assign a different behavioural treatment.

[p181] An Unable to Evaluate Guardrail state must be handled according to PROP-009 and the
[p181] applicable organisational decision requirements rather than being silently interpreted as
[p181] either a pass or a Breach.
[p181] 
[p181] Approval routing must not itself grant approval authority.

[p183]      8.16.      FLOW-016 Approval Binding to Controlled Proposal Version
[p183] 
[p183] 
[p183] Every formal approval decision must bind to the exact controlled Pricing Proposal version
[p183] and decision snapshot submitted into the approval workflow in accordance with PROP-011.
[p183] 
[p183] The approval record defined in FLOW-012 must identify the exact Proposal version against
[p183] which the decision was made.
[p183] 
[p183] The workflow system must not:
[p183] 
[p183]     ● apply an approval made against one Proposal version to another Proposal version;

[p183] 
[p184]    ● allow a mutable Draft Proposal version to receive formal approval;

[p184]        other decision information that changed after submission.
[p184] 
[p184] Where a material change creates a new controlled Proposal version under PROP-017, the
[p184] new version must complete the applicable review and approval requirements independently
[p184] of approvals recorded against the previous version.
[p184] 
[p184] Historical approvals must remain permanently associated with the Proposal version against
[p184] which they were originally made.
[p184]

source.exactNormativeText:
[p184]     8.17.     FLOW-017 Workflow Treatment of Material Proposal Changes
[p184] 
[p184] 
[p184] Where a submitted Pricing Proposal is materially changed in accordance with PROP-017,
[p184] existing approval or policy-authorisation authority must remain applicable only to the
[p184] Proposal version against which that authority was originally established.
[p184] 
[p184] The workflow system must:
[p184] 
[p184]    ● prevent the materially revised pricing action from relying on decision authority
[p184]        attached to the previous Proposal version;
[p184]    ● preserve all reviews, approvals, policy-authorisation records, comments and
[p184]        workflow activity already recorded against the previous version;
[p184]    ● ensure that historical decisions remain bound only to the Proposal version against
[p184]        which they were made;
[p184]    ● require the materially revised pricing work to exist as a new controlled Proposal
[p184]        version;
[p184]    ● determine the applicable organisational decision path for the new Proposal version;
[p184]    ● route the new version through required review and item-level approval where
[p184]        approval is required;
[p184]    ● route the new version through the policy-authorisation evaluation defined in
[p184]        FLOW-022 and FLOW-023 where that path is applicable;
[p184]    ● require the new Proposal version to satisfy its applicable decision requirements
[p184]        before it can become Approved or Authorised Within Policy.
[p184] 
[p184] Previous approvals or policy authorisations must not be transferred, inherited or
[p184] reinterpreted as authority for the materially revised Proposal version.
[p184] 
[p184] The workflow treatment of a material change must remain explicit and auditable.
[p184]

[p184]     8.17.     FLOW-017 Workflow Treatment of Material Proposal Changes
[p184] 
[p184] 
[p184] Where a submitted Pricing Proposal is materially changed in accordance with PROP-017,
[p184] existing approval or policy-authorisation authority must remain applicable only to the
[p184] Proposal version against which that authority was originally established.
[p184] 
[p184] The workflow system must:
[p184] 
[p184]    ● prevent the materially revised pricing action from relying on decision authority
[p184]        attached to the previous Proposal version;
[p184]    ● preserve all reviews, approvals, policy-authorisation records, comments and
[p184]        workflow activity already recorded against the previous version;
[p184]    ● ensure that historical decisions remain bound only to the Proposal version against
[p184]        which they were made;
[p184]    ● require the materially revised pricing work to exist as a new controlled Proposal
[p184]        version;
[p184]    ● determine the applicable organisational decision path for the new Proposal version;
[p184]    ● route the new version through required review and item-level approval where
[p184]        approval is required;
[p184]    ● route the new version through the policy-authorisation evaluation defined in
[p184]        FLOW-022 and FLOW-023 where that path is applicable;
[p184]    ● require the new Proposal version to satisfy its applicable decision requirements
[p184]        before it can become Approved or Authorised Within Policy.
[p184] 
[p184] Previous approvals or policy authorisations must not be transferred, inherited or
[p184] reinterpreted as authority for the materially revised Proposal version.
[p184] 
[p184] The workflow treatment of a material change must remain explicit and auditable.
[p184]

[p185] 
[p185] 
[p185] Where a post-submission change is permitted as non-material in accordance with
[p185] PROP-018, the workflow system may allow the existing review or approval process to
[p185] continue without requiring a new controlled Proposal version.
[p185]

[p185] or change the commercial meaning of the Proposal being reviewed.
[p185]

[p185]

[p185]        approvals apply;

[p185]    ● make the change visible to relevant reviewers or approvers where appropriate;
[p185]    ● preserve the relationship between the change and the affected Proposal version;

[p185]        action, pricing outcome, decision basis or execution instructions.
[p185] 
[p185] Where a change exceeds the non-material boundary defined in PROP-018, it must instead
[p185] be treated as a material Proposal change under PROP-017 and FLOW-017.
[p185] 
[p185] Non-material changes must remain attributable and auditable throughout the applicable
[p185] organisational decision process.
[p185] 
[p185]

[p185] 
[p185]

[p186]        associated with the rejected version;

[p186] organisational decision requirements before execution authority can be established.
[p186] 
[p186] The rejected Proposal version must remain permanently associated with its historical
[p186] workflow and decision record.
[p186]

[p187]      8.22.    FLOW-022 Policy Authorisation Path
[p187] 
[p187] 
[p187] An organisation may optionally configure a policy-authorisation path under which an eligible
[p187] current Draft Pricing Proposal version may receive Authorised Within Policy status without
[p187] item-level human approval.
[p187] 
[p187] This capability must remain disabled unless deliberately configured by an authorised
[p187] organisational user.
[p187] 
[p187] The policy-authorisation path must operate against the exact controlled Proposal version
[p187] and decision snapshot submitted into that path in accordance with PROP-003 and
[p187] PROP-011.
[p187] 
[p187] Policy evaluation must identify, where applicable:
[p187] 
[p187]     ● exact Pricing Proposal version;
[p187]     ● applicable organisational policy;
[p187]     ● qualifying policy conditions;
[p187]     ● authorised Pricing Scope;
[p187]     ● submitting or invoking user and applicable authority;
[p187]     ● applicable Guardrail identifiers and configuration versions preserved under
[p187]         PROP-011;
[p187]     ● applicable ANALYSIS-014 Guardrail evaluation results;
[p187]     ● applicable GOV-025 Guardrail behavioural treatments;
[p187]     ● policy-evaluation result;
[p187] 
[p188]     ● evaluation timestamp.
[p188] 
[p188] The policy-authorisation path must consume the Guardrail configuration and evaluation
[p188] preserved with the controlled Proposal decision snapshot.
[p188] 
[p188] It must not independently recalculate a Guardrail result or replace the preserved Guardrail
[p188] configuration with a later governance configuration.
[p188] 
[p188] Policy-authorisation rules may require particular Guardrail states or behavioural conditions,
[p188] but they must not redefine the Guardrail itself or the deterministic method used to evaluate it.
[p188] 
[p188] Where all applicable policy-authorisation requirements are satisfied, the exact controlled
[p188] Proposal version may receive Authorised Within Policy status in accordance with
[p188] PROP-012.
[p188] 
[p188] Policy authorisation must bind only to that exact controlled Proposal version in accordance
[p188] with PROP-021.
[p188] 
[p188] A later Proposal version, materially revised pricing action or other Pricing Initiative must not
[p188] inherit that policy authorisation.
[p188] 
[p188] Failure and blocking treatment must follow FLOW-023.
[p188] 
[p188]

[p188]      8.23.     FLOW-023 Policy Authorisation Boundary
[p188] 
[p188] 
[p188] A Pricing Proposal version must not receive Authorised Within Policy status where any
[p188] applicable policy-authorisation condition is unsatisfied.
[p188] 
[p188] Blocking conditions must include, where applicable:
[p188] 
[p188]     ● the Proposal does not satisfy PROP-009 decision-readiness requirements;
[p188]     ● the Proposal version is not the Current applicable version;
[p188]     ● required decision information is missing;
[p188]     ● an applicable Guardrail has an ANALYSIS-014 evaluation state of Breach and a
[p188]         GOV-025 behavioural treatment of Blocking;
[p188]     ● a required Guardrail is Unable to Evaluate and the applicable policy does not
[p188]         explicitly permit progression without that evaluation;
[p188]     ● an applicable Guardrail Breach has Approval Escalation treatment and the resulting
[p188]         organisational decision path requires item-level or higher human approval;
[p188]     ● the initiating or submitting user lacks required authority;
[p188] 
[p189]    ● the pricing action exceeds configured policy-authorisation thresholds;
[p189]    ● the Proposal falls outside authorised Pricing Scope;
[p189]    ● the Proposal cannot be reliably evaluated against the configured policy;
[p189]    ● an applicable workflow or governance rule requires explicit item-level approval.
[p189] 
[p189] A Warning Guardrail treatment must not by itself be treated as a Blocking Guardrail
[p189] condition.
[p189] 
[p189] The policy-authorisation evaluation must consume the Guardrail information preserved with
[p189] the exact controlled Proposal version under PROP-011.
[p189] 
[p189] It must not independently calculate another Guardrail result or reinterpret the Proposal using
[p189] a later Guardrail configuration.
[p189] 
[p189] Failure of policy authorisation must not create execution authority or cause the Proposal to
[p189] be represented as Authorised Within Policy.
[p189] 
[p189] Where item-level approval is required, the Proposal must instead enter the applicable
[p189] approval workflow and follow the approval requirements in this section.
[p189] 
[p189] A failed policy-authorisation evaluation must remain attributable and auditable where it
[p189] materially affects Proposal progression.
[p189] 
[p189]

[p188]      8.23.     FLOW-023 Policy Authorisation Boundary
[p188] 
[p188] 
[p188] A Pricing Proposal version must not receive Authorised Within Policy status where any
[p188] applicable policy-authorisation condition is unsatisfied.
[p188] 
[p188] Blocking conditions must include, where applicable:
[p188] 
[p188]     ● the Proposal does not satisfy PROP-009 decision-readiness requirements;
[p188]     ● the Proposal version is not the Current applicable version;
[p188]     ● required decision information is missing;
[p188]     ● an applicable Guardrail has an ANALYSIS-014 evaluation state of Breach and a
[p188]         GOV-025 behavioural treatment of Blocking;
[p188]     ● a required Guardrail is Unable to Evaluate and the applicable policy does not
[p188]         explicitly permit progression without that evaluation;
[p188]     ● an applicable Guardrail Breach has Approval Escalation treatment and the resulting
[p188]         organisational decision path requires item-level or higher human approval;
[p188]     ● the initiating or submitting user lacks required authority;
[p188] 
[p189]    ● the pricing action exceeds configured policy-authorisation thresholds;
[p189]    ● the Proposal falls outside authorised Pricing Scope;
[p189]    ● the Proposal cannot be reliably evaluated against the configured policy;
[p189]    ● an applicable workflow or governance rule requires explicit item-level approval.
[p189] 
[p189] A Warning Guardrail treatment must not by itself be treated as a Blocking Guardrail
[p189] condition.
[p189] 
[p189] The policy-authorisation evaluation must consume the Guardrail information preserved with
[p189] the exact controlled Proposal version under PROP-011.
[p189] 
[p189] It must not independently calculate another Guardrail result or reinterpret the Proposal using
[p189] a later Guardrail configuration.
[p189] 
[p189] Failure of policy authorisation must not create execution authority or cause the Proposal to
[p189] be represented as Authorised Within Policy.
[p189] 
[p189] Where item-level approval is required, the Proposal must instead enter the applicable
[p189] approval workflow and follow the approval requirements in this section.
[p189] 
[p189] A failed policy-authorisation evaluation must remain attributable and auditable where it
[p189] materially affects Proposal progression.
[p189] 
[p189]

[p191]     8.29.      FLOW-029 Workflow Treatment of Expiration
[p191] 
[p191] 
[p191] Pricing Proposal expiration must be represented through Proposal version validity in
[p191] accordance with PROP-013 and PROP-020.
[p191] 
[p191] Where an expiration condition causes the current Proposal version to lose validity for
[p191] progression or execution, the workflow system must:
[p191] 
[p191]    ● prevent that Proposal version from progressing to Ready for Execution or further
[p191]        execution;
[p191]    ● preserve the historical Proposal status and all previous review, Approval and Policy
[p191]        Authorisation records;
[p191]    ● identify the Proposal version as Expired through the canonical Proposal validity
[p191]        model;
[p191]    ● stop or close outstanding workflow actions that no longer remain valid;
[p191]    ● make the expiration condition and required next action visible to relevant users.
[p191] 
[p191] Where organisational policy causes an Approval or Policy Authorisation to cease providing
[p191] current execution authority, the system must preserve the original decision record as
[p191] historical evidence while preventing it from continuing to provide current execution authority.
[p191] 
[p191] Pricing work that has expired must return through the applicable Proposal and decision
[p191] process before new execution authority can be established.
[p191] 
[p191] Expiration must not delete, rewrite or reinterpret the historical decision originally made
[p191] against the Proposal version.
[p191]

[p192]     8.30.          FLOW-030 Execution Readiness Gate
[p192] 
[p192] 
[p192] The workflow system must prevent a Pricing Initiative from entering Ready for Execution
[p192] unless:
[p192] 
[p192]    ● the current applicable Pricing Proposal status is Approved or Authorised Within
[p192]           Policy;
[p192]    ● the applicable Proposal version remains Current and valid for execution in
[p192]           accordance with PROP-013 and PROP-020;
[p192]    ● the exact authorised Proposal version is identifiable as the execution baseline
[p192]           defined in PROP-021;
[p192]    ● all required approval or policy-authorisation conditions have been satisfied;
[p192]    ● no blocking workflow condition remains;
[p192]    ● no blocking governance condition remains;
[p192]    ● no unresolved condition invalidates execution readiness.
[p192] 
[p192] A Superseded, Expired, Rejected, Changes Requested, Awaiting Approval or Draft Proposal
[p192] version must not provide execution authority.
[p192] 
[p192] When the Pricing Initiative progresses to Ready for Execution, the Pricing Proposal must
[p192] retain its existing Approved or Authorised Within Policy status.
[p192] 
[p192] Progression of the Pricing Initiative must not modify, replace or reinterpret the authorised
[p192] Proposal version or its decision snapshot.
[p192] 
[p192] The exact Proposal version that passes the execution-readiness gate must remain the
[p192] authoritative baseline for subsequent execution, export and implementation comparison.
[p192] 
[p192] Execution-readiness validation must consume the exact authorised Proposal version and
[p192] controlled decision snapshot, including the Guardrail configuration and evaluation preserved
[p192] under PROP-011.
[p192] 
[p192] The execution-readiness gate must not independently recalculate Guardrails using later
[p192] workspace       values or substitute a newer Guardrail configuration solely because
[p192] organisational governance has changed after the Proposal decision.
[p192] 
[p192] Where a later governance or Guardrail configuration change is explicitly required to affect
[p192] active pricing work, the resulting treatment must follow GOV-034 and the applicable
[p192] Proposal and workflow requirements before the authoritative execution baseline can change.
[p192] 
[p193] The workflow system must not silently reinterpret an Approved or Authorised Within Policy
[p193] Proposal using governance information that was not part of its controlled decision basis.
[p193] 
[p193]

[p194]     8.35.    FLOW-035 Workflow Configuration Changes
[p194] 
[p194] 
[p194] Consequential changes to a Workflow Configuration Profile must apply prospectively
[p194] according to defined system behaviour.
[p194] 
[p195] Each consequential Workflow Configuration Profile state must remain historically
[p195] distinguishable.
[p195] 
[p195] The system must preserve, where applicable:
[p195] 
[p195]    ● Workflow Configuration Profile identifier;
[p195]    ● configuration version or revision;
[p195]    ● previous configuration state;
[p195]    ● resulting configuration state;
[p195]    ● responsible user;
[p195]    ● change timestamp;
[p195]    ● effective date or effective period where relevant.
[p195] 
[p195] A submitted controlled Pricing Proposal version must remain associated with the exact
[p195] organisational decision path and applicable Workflow Configuration Profile state that formed
[p195] part of its controlled decision context.
[p195] 
[p195] Subsequent Workflow Configuration Profile changes must not silently alter the:
[p195] 
[p195]    ● required review requirements or reviewer actions;
[p195]    ● item-level approval requirements;
[p195]    ● approval sequence;
[p195]    ● policy-authorisation routing treatment;
[p195]    ● approval-routing conditions;
[p195]    ● deadline or escalation treatment;
[p195]    ● authorised-delegation treatment;
[p195]    ● other consequential decision requirements
[p195] 
[p195] applicable to an already submitted Proposal version.
[p195] 
[p195] A Workflow Configuration Profile change must not create new Pricing Initiative lifecycle
[p195] states, redefine canonical lifecycle meaning, redefine Pricing Proposal statuses or validity, or
[p195] introduce capabilities excluded by FLOW-001 and Section 2.4.
[p195] 
[p195] Where a changed Workflow Configuration Profile must affect active pricing work, that
[p195] treatment must be explicit, attributable and auditable and must follow the applicable
[p195] Proposal-version and workflow requirements before the active decision path changes.
[p195] 
[p195] Historical Proposal versions must continue to preserve the exact workflow configuration and
[p195] organisational decision context that applied at the relevant time.
[p195]

[p194]     8.35.    FLOW-035 Workflow Configuration Changes
[p194] 
[p194] 
[p194] Consequential changes to a Workflow Configuration Profile must apply prospectively
[p194] according to defined system behaviour.
[p194] 
[p195] Each consequential Workflow Configuration Profile state must remain historically
[p195] distinguishable.
[p195] 
[p195] The system must preserve, where applicable:
[p195] 
[p195]    ● Workflow Configuration Profile identifier;
[p195]    ● configuration version or revision;
[p195]    ● previous configuration state;
[p195]    ● resulting configuration state;
[p195]    ● responsible user;
[p195]    ● change timestamp;
[p195]    ● effective date or effective period where relevant.
[p195] 
[p195] A submitted controlled Pricing Proposal version must remain associated with the exact
[p195] organisational decision path and applicable Workflow Configuration Profile state that formed
[p195] part of its controlled decision context.
[p195] 
[p195] Subsequent Workflow Configuration Profile changes must not silently alter the:
[p195] 
[p195]    ● required review requirements or reviewer actions;
[p195]    ● item-level approval requirements;
[p195]    ● approval sequence;
[p195]    ● policy-authorisation routing treatment;
[p195]    ● approval-routing conditions;
[p195]    ● deadline or escalation treatment;
[p195]    ● authorised-delegation treatment;
[p195]    ● other consequential decision requirements
[p195] 
[p195] applicable to an already submitted Proposal version.
[p195] 
[p195] A Workflow Configuration Profile change must not create new Pricing Initiative lifecycle
[p195] states, redefine canonical lifecycle meaning, redefine Pricing Proposal statuses or validity, or
[p195] introduce capabilities excluded by FLOW-001 and Section 2.4.
[p195] 
[p195] Where a changed Workflow Configuration Profile must affect active pricing work, that
[p195] treatment must be explicit, attributable and auditable and must follow the applicable
[p195] Proposal-version and workflow requirements before the active decision path changes.
[p195] 
[p195] Historical Proposal versions must continue to preserve the exact workflow configuration and
[p195] organisational decision context that applied at the relevant time.
[p195]

[p206]     9.23.     GOV-023 Guardrail Definition and Management Authority
[p206] 
[p206] 
[p206] Only authorised administrative or policy-management users may create, modify, activate or
[p206] deactivate organisational pricing guardrails.
[p206] 
[p206] A Guardrail is a configured organisational pricing constraint used to evaluate whether
[p206] proposed pricing work remains within an acceptable pricing boundary.
[p206] 
[p206] A Guardrail must remain distinct from:
[p206] 
[p206]    ● approval authority;
[p206]    ● approval-routing thresholds;
[p206]    ● workflow-routing rules;
[p206]    ● policy-authorisation eligibility;
[p206]    ● user permissions;
[p206]    ● initiative-specific assumptions or commercial targets.
[p206] 
[p206] Supported organisational guardrails for the MVP may include, where applicable:
[p206] 
[p206]    ● minimum gross-margin threshold;
[p206]    ● maximum discount;
[p206]    ● maximum price increase;
[p206]    ● maximum price decrease;
[p206]    ● maximum absolute or percentage price movement;
[p206]    ● another supported pricing constraint that can be evaluated from structured pricing
[p206]        information.
[p206] 
[p206] Each configured Guardrail must identify, where applicable:
[p206] 
[p206]    ● persistent Guardrail identifier;
[p206]    ● name or human-readable description;
[p206]    ● guardrail type;
[p206]    ● metric or pricing condition being evaluated;
[p206]    ● operator or comparison rule;
[p206]    ● threshold or configured value;
[p206]    ● applicable organisational or Pricing Scope;
[p206]    ● applicable pricing dimensions where relevant;
[p206]

[p207]     9.24.     GOV-024 Guardrail Enforcement and Ownership Boundary
[p207] 
[p207] 
[p207] Applicable organisational Guardrails must be enforced consistently wherever consequential
[p207] pricing work is performed.
[p207] 
[p207] Governance must determine:
[p207] 
[p207]    ● which configured Guardrails apply to the pricing work;
[p207]    ● which Guardrail configuration version applies;
[p207]    ● the applicable scope and pricing dimensions;
[p207] 
[p208]    ● the behavioural treatment configured under GOV-025.
[p208] 
[p208] Deterministic evaluation of an applicable Guardrail against pricing values or calculated
[p208] outcomes must be performed by the analytical layer in accordance with ANALYSIS-014.
[p208] 
[p208] Governance must consume the resulting analytical Guardrail evaluation rather than
[p208] independently calculating a second Guardrail result.
[p208] 
[p208] The same applicable Guardrail configuration and evaluation result must be consumed
[p208] consistently by:
[p208] 
[p208]    ● Pricing Builder;
[p208]    ● analysis and Scenarios;
[p208]    ● Proposal readiness and submission;
[p208]    ● review;
[p208]    ● item-level approval routing where relevant;
[p208]    ● policy-authorisation evaluation;
[p208]    ● execution readiness;
[p208]    ● historical reconstruction.
[p208] 
[p208] A user must not be able to obtain a different Guardrail outcome merely by moving pricing
[p208] work between product surfaces.
[p208] 
[p208] Where decision-relevant pricing inputs change while the work remains editable, applicable
[p208] Guardrail evaluations must be refreshed using the analytical layer.
[p208] 
[p208] Where a Pricing Proposal has already been submitted, subsequent Guardrail configuration
[p208] changes must not silently replace or reinterpret the Guardrail configuration and evaluation
[p208] preserved with that controlled Proposal version.
[p208] 
[p208] Guardrail definition, applicability and behavioural treatment remain governed by Section 3.9.
[p208] 
[p208] Guardrail calculation and evaluation remain governed by Section 3.5.
[p208]

[p208]     9.25.      GOV-025 Guardrail Behavioural Treatment
[p208] 
[p208] 
[p208] Each configured Guardrail must have a supported behavioural treatment that determines the
[p208] governance consequence of a confirmed Guardrail Breach.
[p208] 
[p208] Supported MVP treatments must include:
[p208] 
[p209] Warning
[p209] 
[p209] A confirmed Breach may continue through the pricing process where other applicable
[p209] requirements are satisfied, but the Breach must remain prominently visible to relevant users
[p209] and within the decision record.
[p209] 
[p209] Approval Escalation
[p209] 
[p209] A confirmed Breach requires the pricing work to follow the configured higher or additional
[p209] approval path before organisational decision authority can be established.
[p209] 
[p209] Approval Escalation must not itself grant approval authority or determine which user may

[p211]     9.28.      GOV-028 Policy Authorisation Governance Enforcement
[p211] 
[p211] 
[p211] When a Pricing Proposal enters the policy-authorisation path, the governance system must
[p211] enforce the organisational authority and configuration applicable to that decision path.
[p211] 
[p211] Governance evaluation must verify, where applicable:
[p211] 
[p211]    ● that the policy-authorisation capability is enabled;
[p211]    ● that the applicable policy exists and is currently valid;
[p211]    ● that the submitting or invoking user possesses the required authority;
[p211]    ● that the Pricing Proposal falls within the user's permitted organisational and pricing
[p211]        scope;
[p211]    ● that the applicable policy and guardrail configuration may be applied to the Proposal;
[p211]    ● that no permission or governance restriction requires the action to be rejected from
[p211]        the policy-authorisation path.
[p211] 
[p211] Where Guardrails form part of policy-authorisation qualification, governance evaluation must
[p211] consume:
[p211] 
[p211]    ● applicable Guardrail identifiers;
[p211]    ● applicable Guardrail configuration versions;
[p211]    ● applicable GOV-025 behavioural treatments;
[p211] 
[p212]     ● authoritative ANALYSIS-014 evaluation results preserved with the exact controlled
[p212]          Proposal decision snapshot under PROP-011.
[p212] 
[p212] GOV-028 must not perform a separate quantitative Guardrail calculation or substitute a later
[p212] Guardrail configuration for the configuration preserved with the submitted Proposal version.
[p212] 
[p212] A policy condition may require a particular Guardrail evaluation state or behavioural
[p212] treatment, but the Guardrail definition, deterministic evaluation, and behavioural treatment
[p212] must remain owned by their canonical functional requirements.
[p212] 
[p212] A user must not be able to obtain policy authorisation by modifying their own role, scope,
