source.exactNormativeText:
[p214]     9.34.     GOV-034 Governance Configuration Versioning and Historical Context
[p214] 
[p214] 
[p214] Consequential governance configuration must remain historically traceable.
[p214] 
[p214] The system must preserve consequential changes to supported governance configuration
[p214] including:
[p214] 
[p214]    ● roles;
[p214]    ● permissions;
[p214]    ● approval authority and limits;
[p214]    ● Guardrails;
[p214]    ● workflow policies;
[p214]    ● scope assignments;
[p214]    ● policy-authorisation configuration and conditions.
[p214] 
[p214] For each consequential governance configuration change, the system must preserve, where
[p214] applicable:
[p214] 
[p214]    ● affected configuration object;
[p214]    ● persistent configuration identifier;
[p214]    ● configuration version or revision;
[p214]    ● previous configuration state;
[p214]    ● resulting configuration state;
[p214]    ● responsible user;
[p214]    ● change timestamp;
[p214]    ● effective date or effective period where relevant.
[p214] 
[p215] For Guardrails specifically, each consequential configuration state must remain identifiable
[p215] through the persistent Guardrail identifier and the applicable configuration version or
[p215] revision.
[p215] 
[p215] A change to a Guardrail threshold, operator, applicable scope, behavioural treatment,
[p215] effective period or active status must create historically distinguishable governance
[p215] configuration.
[p215] 
[p215] Submitted Pricing Proposal versions must remain associated with the exact governance and
[p215] Guardrail configuration that formed part of their controlled decision snapshot.
[p215] 
[p215] A later governance configuration change must not silently rewrite:
[p215] 
[p215]    ● an earlier Proposal decision snapshot;
[p215]    ● the Guardrail evaluation preserved with that Proposal;
[p215]    ● a historical approval or policy authorisation;
[p215]    ● the governance context under which an earlier decision occurred.
[p215] 
[p215] Where a changed governance configuration must affect active pricing work, the resulting
[p215] treatment must be explicit, attributable and auditable and must follow the applicable
[p215] Proposal, workflow and governance requirements.
[p215] 
[p215] Historical pricing decisions must remain sufficient to determine which governance
[p215] configuration applied at the relevant time.
[p215] 
[p215]

source.exactNormativeText:
[p220]     10.7.       AI-007 Natural Language to Structured Pricing Logic
[p220] 
[p220] 
[p220] Users should be able to describe pricing intent in natural language and request AI
[p220] assistance in translating it into supported Pricing Builder structures.
[p220] 
[p220] For example:
[p220] 
[p220] "Increase prices for these products by 5%, but do not allow gross margin to fall below
[p220] 18%."
[p220] 
[p220] AI may translate this into structured:
[p220] 
[p220]    ● pricing action;
[p220]    ● affected scope;
[p220]    ● percentage adjustment;
[p220]    ● initiative-specific margin constraint or reference to an applicable organisational
[p220]         Guardrail;
[p220]    ● applicable conditions.
[p220] 
[p220] Natural-language pricing intent must not cause AI to create or modify an organisational
[p220] Guardrail through ordinary Pricing Builder work.
[p220] 
[p221] Where the user's instruction describes a pricing boundary that is not already represented by
[p221] an applicable organisational Guardrail, AI may translate that boundary into an
[p221] initiative-specific condition or constraint.
[p221] 
[p221] That condition or constraint must remain distinguishable from an organisational Guardrail.
[p221] 
[p221] Where an applicable organisational Guardrail already exists, AI may reference it but must
[p221] not redefine its threshold, scope, configuration version or behavioural treatment.
[p221] 
[p221] Creation or modification of an organisational Guardrail requires the authorised governance
[p221] process defined in GOV-023.
[p221] 
[p221] The user must review and explicitly apply the resulting structure.
[p221] 
[p221]

Must.snippet: The resulting Price Record must identify, where applicable: ● affected Priceable Entity; ● actual implemented price; ● currency; ● applicable pricing dimensions; ● actual effective date or timestamp; ● originating Pricing Initiative; ● authorised Pricing Propo…

Where the previous Current Price has an open-ended or overlapping effective period, establishing the implemented Price Record as the new Current Price must end the previous record's current applicability from the applicable new effective time.
This transition must preserve the previous Price Record and its historical period of applicability rather than rewriting the previous selling-price value.
The system must therefore be able to distinguish: ● the Price Record that applied before implementation; ● the effective transition point; ● the Price Record that applies after implementation.
The previous Price Record must remain historically preserved.

Where implementation affects only part of an authorised Pricing Scope, Current Price must be updated only for the Priceable Entities and pricing-dimension combinations actually confirmed as implemented.

…l implemented price differs materially from the authorised pricing value, the system must preserve that difference through the applicable execution-variance requirements before treating the implemented value as an ordinary authorised implementation outcome.
The resulting Current Price must remain traceable to the implementation event that established it.

Must Not.snippet: Establishing the implemented price as Current Price must not overwrite the Price Record representing the previous Current Price.
Updating effective applicability to reflect that transition must not destroy the historical state that existed before the implemented price became effective.

A Current Price update must not silently modify: ● the authorised Pricing Proposal version; ● its submitted decision snapshot; ● the authorised pricing value; ● the historical current price used as the decision baseline.

Where implementation occurs outside Owómidé, the workspace must not represent the new value as Current Price until implementation has been recorded or confirmed through the applicable execution process.

domainMatrixEvidence.exactRequirementText:
11.14.       EXEC-014 Current Price Update

Where implementation is confirmed and the applicable organisation pricing record is
maintained inside Owómidé, the system should allow the actual implemented selling price to
establish or update the applicable Price Record.

The resulting Price Record must identify, where applicable:

   ● affected Priceable Entity;
   ● actual implemented price;
   ● currency;
   ● applicable pricing dimensions;
   ● actual effective date or timestamp;
   ● originating Pricing Initiative;
   ● authorised Pricing Proposal version;
   ● Execution Record;
   ● implementing or confirming user;

   ● source and provenance.

Where the implemented price becomes presently applicable to that exact pricing context, the
resulting Price Record should become the Current Price in accordance with DATA-003.

Establishing the implemented price as Current Price must not overwrite the Price Record
representing the previous Current Price.

Where the previous Current Price has an open-ended or overlapping effective period,
establishing the implemented Price Record as the new Current Price must end the previous
record's current applicability from the applicable new effective time.

This transition must preserve the previous Price Record and its historical period of
applicability rather than rewriting the previous selling-price value.

The system must therefore be able to distinguish:

   ● the Price Record that applied before implementation;
   ● the effective transition point;
   ● the Price Record that applies after implementation.

Updating effective applicability to reflect that transition must not destroy the historical state
that existed before the implemented price became effective.

The previous Price Record must remain historically preserved.

Where implementation affects only part of an authorised Pricing Scope, Current Price must
be updated only for the Priceable Entities and pricing-dimension combinations actually
confirmed as implemented.

Where the actual implemented price differs materially from the authorised pricing value, the
system    must    preserve   that    difference   through    the applicable execution-variance
requirements     before   treating   the   implemented      value   as an ordinary authorised
implementation outcome.

A Current Price update must not silently modify:

   ● the authorised Pricing Proposal version;
   ● its submitted decision snapshot;
   ● the authorised pricing value;
   ● the historical current price used as the decision baseline.

Where implementation occurs outside Owómidé, the workspace must not represent the new
value as Current Price until implementation has been recorded or confirmed through the
applicable execution process.

The resulting Current Price must remain traceable to the implementation event that
established it.

11.30.     EXEC-030 Execution and Monitoring Completeness Principle

The pricing lifecycle is not complete merely because a Pricing Proposal becomes Approved
or Authorised Within Policy.

The MVP must preserve an intelligible chain from:

Proposed Pricing Action → Organisational Decision Authority → Actual Implementation →
Observed Outcome

For every consequential pricing action, the organisation must be able to distinguish:

   ● what was proposed;
   ● which exact Pricing Proposal version received execution authority;
   ● whether that authority resulted from approval or policy authorisation;
   ● what was actually implemented;
   ● whether implementation differed from the authorised decision baseline;
   ● what outcome was subsequently recorded.

Proposal decision status, execution status and observed outcome must remain separate
concepts.

The system must not imply that authorisation guarantees implementation or that
implementation guarantees the intended commercial outcome.

[p252] 
[p252] 
[p252] For every submitted Pricing Proposal version, the system must preserve the complete
[p252] controlled decision snapshot established under PROP-011 as part of the Pricing Initiative's
[p252] historical record.
[p252] 
[p252] The historical record must preserve the Proposal snapshot exactly as it existed when that
[p252] version was submitted, including its relationships to the underlying pricing context, analysis,
[p252] assumptions, evidence, guardrail evaluation and other decision-relevant source objects.
[p252] 
[p252] Subsequent changes to:
[p252] 
[p252]     ● current prices;
[p252] 
[p253]    ● costs or other financial inputs;
[p253]    ● pricing context;
[p253]    ● Pricing Builder logic;
[p253]    ● assumptions;
[p253]    ● analysis;
[p253]    ● evidence;
[p253]    ● guardrails;
[p253]    ● workflow or governance configuration;
[p253]    ● other workspace data
[p253] 
[p253] must not modify, recalculate or reinterpret the historical Proposal decision snapshot.
[p253] 
[p253] Where a referenced source object changes after submission, the historical Proposal version
[p253] must continue to resolve to the version or value that formed part of its original decision
[p253] snapshot.
[p253] 
[p253] Historical preservation must not independently redefine the contents of the Proposal
[p253] decision snapshot. The canonical snapshot contract is governed by PROP-011.
[p253]

12.26.         HIST-026 System Event Recording

System-enforced events that materially affect consequential pricing work should be recorded
where relevant.

Examples include:

   ● creation of a new controlled Pricing Proposal version following a material
       post-submission change;
   ● policy-authorisation        evaluation   where the result materially affects Proposal
       progression;
   ● guardrail      evaluation    that   blocks, escalates or otherwise materially affects
       progression;
   ● Pricing Proposal expiration;
   ● workflow escalation;
   ● prevention of execution or operational export because current execution authority is
       invalid;
   ● permission-based action denial where organisational audit policy requires it.

A system-generated event must identify the affected pricing object and relevant version
where applicable.

System-event history must record what occurred without independently redefining the
underlying Proposal, workflow, governance, guardrail, execution or permission rule that
caused the event.

Historical approval or policy-authorisation records must not be described as deleted or
retrospectively invalidated merely because a later Proposal version is created. Their

[p276] 
[p276]

[p276]

[p276]

[p276]

[p276]     ● Changes Requested;
[p276]     ● Rejected;
[p276]     ● Approved;
[p276]     ● Authorised Within Policy.
[p276] 
[p276] Where Pricing Proposal Version Validity is included, the exported value must use the

[p276] 
[p276]     ● Current;
[p276]     ● Superseded;
[p276]     ● Expired.
[p276] 
[p276] Proposal Version Validity must not be merged into or represented as Pricing Proposal
[p276] Status.
[p276]

[p277] applicable execution states defined in EXEC-010:
[p277] 
[p277]     ● Not Started;
[p277]     ● In Progress;
[p277]     ● Partially Implemented;
[p277]     ● Implemented;

[p277] must preserve both pieces of information rather than replacing its historical Proposal status

14.28.     EXPORT-028 Bounded External Integration

The MVP must support bounded integration with selected external systems where those
integrations materially improve the ability to exchange pricing context or authorised pricing
work with the organisation's existing operating environment.

Supported integrations may include selected:

   ● spreadsheet and productivity systems;
   ● ERP platforms;
   ● commerce or marketplace platforms;
   ● other business systems required by validated MVP customers.

An integration may support inbound data exchange, outbound authorised pricing handoff or
both, according to the capabilities of the supported connector.

The MVP is not required to provide broad connector coverage, universal bidirectional
synchronisation or autonomous execution across an organisation's technology stack.

Where a native connector is unavailable, the customer must remain able to complete the
core Owómidé pricing workflow through supported manual entry, structured import, export
and operational handoff mechanisms.

Specific integrations must be prioritised according to validated customer and pilot
requirements rather than treated as universal MVP dependencies.
